text:
On the morning of 14 March 2031, the control room at the Halvern Deep-Sea Institute was quiet in the way rooms are when people are waiting on something they cannot hurry. Screens glowed with a single descending line. After 6 hours and 52 minutes, the Marisol Trench probe reached 9,400 metres, its maximum depth, and sent its final reading.

For decades the trench was known mostly through inference, a dark gap on charts filled in by sonar and educated guesswork. Mission MT-7 changed that. Dr. Ilvane Corsetti, the lead mission oceanographer, had spent years preparing for this moment.

The Institute set out the findings in its "Marisol Trench Descent Report (Mission MT-7)," released at a press briefing on 16 March 2031. It is a sober document, and it leaves the reader thinking about how much remains unseen.
